newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA still sees differences on Airbus.
newsitem.headline: DASA still sees differences on Airbus.

text.p: Differences remain among the partners in the Airbus consortium despite the signing of a deal on Monday by its four members to restructure the group by 1999, DASA chairman Manfred Bischoff said.
Bischoff told reporters there were still different views over the amount of productive assets that should be brought in to the limited liability company which is to replace the existing partnership.
Bischoff said DASA, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, was "top fit" and ready to join the new Airbus structure.
Earlier, in a magazine interview, Bischoff had called on and British Aerospace to help the new company achieve a return on equity of 12 percent.
The fourth partner in the consortium is Spain's CASA.

Bischoff said that the restructuring should ready Airbus for a stock market listing in the long term, and said that bringing in new partners -- such as U.S. Lockheed Martin or interests from the former Soviet Union -- was possible.

Bischoff confirmed earlier news that separate bilateral projects between DASA and Aerospatiale in satellite and missile development had been put "on ice" due to funding difficulties and a lack of progress in Franco-German military cooperation.
